title: David Obie and Jenny Dillard
summary: David Obie was the waiter who helped; Jenny Dillard came to New York with her and worked at the Onyx Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Can you tell us a little bit about these figures who kind of come into your biography and they kind of fade away again? First of all David Obie.

Yeah, David Obje was the waiter. He was the waiter at the Benjamin Harrison Literary Club. And he was the strong fan of the swinger. He would come in every night and rave about the shows he heard, Benny Goodman. In fact I think he came to New York to catch the band at different times. He was not a performer himself but he was a very good waiter and very popular around the club. He knew all the entertainers.
No he was white. I think Dave

had a brother here in New York that was very active with a Catholic Youth Organization, because later on when I came to New York he made himself known to me and I found out that this was David Obie's brother.
That's all I knew about Dave.

Jenny came to New York with me and we worked at the Onyx Club in the beginning during intermission. And I'd say about a month. And then of course after Clauda arranged some other things for me I began to appear with the band, with John Kirby's Orchestra. And Jenny continued to play intermission. And she was there, well the whole time I was there, but what happened was, I became, after having done 'Loch Lomond' I became very popular and I left the Onyx Club and went out to Hollywood. Jenny didn't want to travel with me at the time. Then when I came back Jenny was no longer

at the Onyx Club. She was working around New York with some other singers. I understood that later on she formed a combination of her own but I lost track of Jenny until about 1942 I was able to contact Jenny and I tried to interest her in working with me, you know, probably going out and helping me out with some of my engagements, because by that time I was using big band arrangements. It wasn't an act anymore but I figured that she could go along with me. She could always be my piano player, by my musical director. But she wasn't particularly interested so I had to just let that drop. I don't know what has happened to Jenny. I don't know whether she's still around New York or not, but I lost track of her. But we came to New York together and we auditioned and went to work at the Onyx Club and did intermission for about, I'd say about three or four months. And then Claude made the arrangement and I started playing with the band. Anybody else that you're . . .
